# Shift Handover

Fifteen minutes before the change, the outgoing crew writes a logbook entry
covering four things: the machine state as it stands, anything that was trimmed
away from the standard setup, any equipment left tagged out, and any beamline
that reported a problem during the shift.

The incoming crew reads that entry, walks the alarm summary with the outgoing
operator still present, and only then signs the console over. Nothing is handed
over verbally alone.

The console binder carries the escalation list. First contact is the on-call
accelerator physicist, reachable around the clock on the duty pager; radio-frequency
and cryogenic faults escalate directly to their own on-call engineer instead. For
anything that has already dropped the stored beam twice in a shift, the operations
manager is paged regardless of the hour.

Handover during a maintenance period additionally lists every access permit still
open and who holds each key.
